correctness.rationale: The midpoint M and difference D are independent nondegenerate Gaussians. The exact projection identity gives the risk formula by zeroing the M cross term. Its derivative is the strictly positive Gaussian integral multiplied by the sign of lambda-2sigma², proving the unique optimum. Density positivity at D=0 yields the complete q-moment threshold, and conditional dominated convergence gives the exact tail coefficient. Pointwise fraction identities and Gaussian quadrature were executed from verify.py.

value.rationale: Regularization strength is an essential practical decision in noise-sensitive Anderson residual projection. This result identifies an exact nonasymptotic variance-only calibration independent of unknown slope/spacing in a natural balanced local test, and exhibits a strong quantitative contrast with the unregularized infinite-moment pole even for tiny noise. It is not advertised as globally estimator-optimal or as an implementable method to choose probes around an unknown root. This precisely scoped complete risk classification informs stabilization benchmarks rather than merely renaming a textbook normal-ratio distribution.
